ANUPAM RASAYAN Q2 FY27: SIGNS 6-YEAR US SUPPLY AGREEMENT; ACQUIRES 50.07% STAKE IN BLISS GVS PHARMA, EXPANDS INTO PHARMACEUTICAL FORMULATIONS

• New US Supply Agreement: Signed a six-year long-term supply agreement with a US-based specialty metal manufacturer, marking its entry into the geological resources sector.

• Strategic Acquisition: Completed acquisition of a 50.07% controlling stake in Bliss GVS Pharma, strengthening its pharmaceutical business.

• Pharmaceutical Expansion: Acquisition adds finished dosage formulation capabilities, enabling expansion across the pharmaceutical value chain.

• Global Customer Expansion: Focused on deepening relationships with existing international customers and expanding into new applications and end markets.

• Business Diversification: Strengthening capabilities across Pharmaceuticals, Performance Materials and other specialised chemical segments.

• Acquisition Synergies: Management expects operational and commercial synergies from integrating Bliss GVS Pharma with its existing businesses.

• Manufacturing Strategy: Prioritising optimal utilisation of capital employed and continuous improvement in manufacturing and technological capabilities.

• Future Growth Strategy: Building a globally integrated specialty chemicals and pharmaceutical platform through strategic investments, new applications and customer diversification.

WEST COAST PAPER Q2: APPROVES ₹290 CR OPTICAL FIBRE EXPANSION; TO NEARLY DOUBLE CAPACITY

• Capex Approval: Board approved ₹290 Cr investment to expand Optical Fibre (OF) and Optical Fibre Cable (OFC) manufacturing capacity at West Coast Optilinks

• Optical Fibre Capacity: To increase from 4.0 Mn FKM to 8.0 Mn FKM annually, a 100% expansion

• Optical Fibre Cable Capacity: To increase from 4.2 Mn FKM to 7.3 Mn FKM annually, adding 3.1 Mn FKM (+73.8%)

• Commissioning Timeline: Additional manufacturing capacity expected to be operational by Q3 FY29

• Existing Utilisation: FY26 production utilisation stood at 2.9 Mn FKM for Optical Fibre and 2.3 Mn FKM for Optical Fibre Cable

• Funding: Expansion to be financed through internal accruals and/or debt from banks and financial institutions

• AI & Data Centres: Expansion targets rising demand from hyperscale data centres and AI-enabled digital infrastructure

• Telecom Opportunity: Higher capacity expected to support telecom network expansion and modernisation

• Defence Applications: Additional manufacturing capabilities also target growing demand from defence applications

• Product Expansion: Plans to introduce a new product line in the Optical Fibre Cable segment

• Export Opportunities: Higher manufacturing scale expected to improve export competitiveness and strengthen international market presence

• Growth Outlook: Expansion aims to improve operational efficiency, economies of scale and supply-chain capabilities

• Capital Allocation: Continuing strategic growth investments while maintaining focus on leverage and operating cash generation.

HONASA CONSUMER Q2 FY27: EYES ₹7,000–7,500 CR HAIR COLOUR MARKET; PREMIUM BEAUTY, OFFLINE DISTRIBUTION & YOUNGER BRANDS EXPANSION IN FOCUS

• Hair Colour Opportunity: Management identifies India's ₹7,000–7,500 Cr+ organised hair colour market as an attractive category, with newer formats growing at mid-teens CAGR.

• Hair Colour Strategy: Highlighting a consumer shift from traditional grey coverage towards styling, crème-based formats, non-black colours and safer, ammonia-free products.

• Mamaearth Growth Strategy: Focused on sustaining its high-teens growth trajectory while maintaining a mid-teens brand-level EBITDA margin profile.

• Younger Brands Expansion: Scaling The Derma Co., Aqualogica, Dr. Sheth's, BBlunt, Staze and Reginald Men through premium products and wider distribution.

• Offline Distribution: Strengthening general trade penetration, increasing productivity per retail outlet and expanding modern trade coverage.

• The Derma Co. Expansion: Focused on expanding its offline network and strengthening the brand's presence in face cleansers and science-led skincare.

• BBlunt Growth Strategy: Expanding its hair colour and hair care portfolio, supported by the relaunched Salon Secret High Shine Hair Colour range.

• Premium Skincare Innovation: Dr. Sheth's expanding into advanced formulations, including Bakuchiol, PDRN, collagen and peptide-based skincare.

• Aqualogica Expansion: Developing moisturisers, body mists and multifunctional sun protection products to capture emerging beauty trends.

• Staze Cosmetics: Focused on scaling its hero products and expanding multifunctional colour cosmetics.

• Reginald Men: Developing face wash as a second key product category within its men's grooming portfolio.

• Margin Strategy: Prioritising advertising efficiency, a higher contribution from profitable offline and quick-commerce B2B channels, and operating leverage.

• Future Growth Plans: Increasing penetration across face cleansers, shampoos, serums, sunscreens, moisturisers, baby care and colour cosmetics.

ANUP ENGINEERING Q2 FY27: TARGETS 20% REVENUE GROWTH IN FY28; ₹941 CR ORDER BOOK, ₹1,200 CR ORDER PIPELINE & CLEAN ENERGY STORAGE TO CONTRIBUTE 20% REVENUE

• FY28 Revenue Growth Target: Management targets approximately 20% revenue growth next year, supported by order enquiries across Oil & Gas, Fertilizers, Thermal Power and Clean Energy Storage.

• Strong Order Book: Pending order book, including Letters of Intent (LOIs), stands at ₹941 Cr as of November 6, 2026, with approximately ₹390 Cr scheduled for FY28.

• Order Enquiry Pipeline: Active enquiries worth ₹1,200 Cr provide opportunities for additional order wins in the coming months.

• Thermal Power Orders: Secured orders exceeding ₹150 Cr for critical heat exchangers used in thermal power plants.

• Thermal Power Outlook: Management expects strong demand from thermal power projects for at least the next three years.

• Clean Energy Storage Guidance: Management expects clean energy storage projects, particularly in the US, to contribute approximately 20% of total revenue in FY28.

• Technical Services Revenue Target: Expects approximately ₹50 Cr revenue during FY27 from technical and site services, with three site execution projects underway.

• New Proprietary Products: Plans to add five proprietary equipment products to its portfolio during FY27, strengthening its positioning as a Tier-1 supplier.

• High-Value Product Orders: Secured orders for three proprietary licensed products, supporting expansion into specialised engineering segments.

• Domestic Business Outlook: Domestic orders account for 67% of the pending order book, while exports contribute 33%, indicating improving domestic demand.

• Manufacturing Expansion: Kheda facility's Phase 3 expansion, comprising three additional production bays, remains part of future development plans. No commissioning date specified.

• FY27 Management Outlook: Prioritising operational stabilisation, better execution, consolidation, profitability and risk mitigation amid geopolitical uncertainty.

• Margin Challenges: Elevated raw material costs and geopolitical disruptions remain key risks. Management is prioritising disciplined pricing and profitable order execution.

BANSAL ROOFING PRODUCTS Q2 FY27: ₹25–30 CR NEW PANEL PLANT PLANNED; PHASE 5 & 6 EXPANSION TARGETED BY MID-NOVEMBER 2026, 200 MT MONTHLY CAPACITY ADDITION

• New Capex Project: Management plans ₹25–30 Cr investment in a continuous insulated panel manufacturing facility to expand its building solutions portfolio.

• New Manufacturing Venture: Proposed plant to be established through Durapuf Insutech Panels Pvt. Ltd., a planned venture between Bansal Roofing and an individual partner.

• Commissioning Timeline: New insulated panel facility targets commercial production by late CY2027; land selection and machinery procurement are being finalised.

• Phase 5 & 6 Expansion: Construction progressing at Vadodara, with both manufacturing expansions targeted for completion by mid-November 2026.

• Capacity Addition: Phase 6 expected to add approximately 200 MT per month of light-fabrication Pre-Engineered Building (PEB) manufacturing capacity once fully operational.

• Solar Business Expansion: Entered Solar Module Mounting Structures (MMS) manufacturing, with a dedicated high-speed roll-forming line already operational.

• Renewable Energy Growth Strategy: Expanding its solar structures business through dedicated marketing personnel, industry exhibitions and customer acquisition initiatives.

• Manufacturing Efficiency: Focused on higher capacity utilisation, two-shift production, machinery upgrades, reduced scrap generation and faster project execution.

• Captive Solar Power: Rooftop solar capacity stands at 300 kW, meeting approximately 53% of factory power requirements.

• Future Growth Plans: Targeting opportunities across industrial buildings, warehousing, infrastructure, solar mounting structures and insulated building panels.

• FY27 Capex Guidance: No separate annual capex budget .The ₹25–30 Cr insulated panel project is a proposed investment with a late-CY2027 commissioning target.

OPTIEMUS INFRACOM Q2 FY27: UPGRADES FY28 REVENUE GUIDANCE TO ₹6,500 CR & FY29 TO ₹8,500 CR; ₹250–300 CR SCREEN PROTECTOR CAPEX, 2.5 CR MONTHLY CAPACITY TARGET

• FY27 Revenue Guidance Maintained: Management expects revenue of approximately ₹3,600 Cr, nearly double FY26, driven primarily by EMS manufacturing expansion

• FY28 Guidance Upgraded: Revenue target raised to ₹6,500 Cr, implying approximately 80% YoY growth versus 30% growth guided earlier

• FY29 Guidance Upgraded: Revenue target raised to ₹8,500 Cr from ₹6,000 Cr earlier, supported by EMS expansion and commercialisation of the screen protector business

• Major Capex Expansion: Plans ₹250–300 Cr investment in screen protector manufacturing, targeting combined monthly production capacity of 2.5 Cr units

• Fundraising Plans: Approximately ₹200 Cr proposed to be raised through further securities issuance, with remaining expansion funding through debt and internal accruals. Management indicates promoter participation

• Brownfield Capacity Expansion: Existing Noida screen protector capacity to increase from 20 lakh to 50 lakh units per month, targeting January–February 2027

• New Greenfield Plant: Plans 2 Cr screen protectors per month capacity at a leased, preconstructed facility in Noida, targeting operations by March 2027

• BIS Regulatory Opportunity: Screen protector BIS and fog-marking requirements are scheduled to become effective April 1, 2027, creating an import substitution opportunity

• Screen Protector Market: Management estimates the existing import-led market at ₹20,000 Cr at consumer prices, with potential to reach ₹40,000 Cr by 2030

• New Consumer Brands: Developing SCREENlife, OPTIGUARD, RHINOTECH and KAVACH screen protection products, including an insurance-backed display protection offering

• Nothing–CMF Joint Venture: Proposed approximately 51:49 JV between Optiemus and Nothing to develop CMF as an independent consumer electronics brand with in-house design, engineering, R&D, sales and marketing capabilities

• CMF Manufacturing Opportunity: Optiemus expects its EMS division to undertake manufacturing for the proposed JV, supporting additional manufacturing volumes. Definitive agreement and regulatory approvals remain pending

• Second B2C Product Launch: Plans to introduce another consumer product category in Q4 FY27, leveraging existing manufacturing capabilities and distribution networks

• Corning Cover Glass JV: 70:30 JV with Corning has its Tamil Nadu manufacturing facility ready; OEM audits and technical trials underway

• Cover Glass Commercialisation: Customer onboarding expected from Q1 FY28, with management indicating a 3–4 quarter onboarding window

• EMS Expansion: Scaling smartphone manufacturing, IoT modules, power banks, POS devices and non-mobile electronics, supported by Unit 3 production ramp-up

• Drone Business: Developing high-altitude defence and precision-agriculture platforms, targeting long-term rental and service contracts with government and defence customers

• Drone Revenue Opportunity: Management has not included potential drone business contributions in its existing revenue guidance

• Growth Strategy: Transitioning from contract electronics manufacturing towards an integrated EMS, components and branded consumer technology business

KSH INTERNATIONAL – CONCALL KEY TAKEAWAYS

REVENUE & EBITDA OUTLOOK
- ₹1 lakh/tonne is peak, not sustainable floor.
- Long-term realisation target: ₹85,000/tonne.
- Assumes full capacity utilisation.
- CTC mix, exports and weak rupee boosted realisations.
- Blended margins expected to decline in H2.
- Standard wire will fill new production lines.
- Absolute EBITDA expected to remain stable.
- Volume growth guidance maintained at 25–26%.
- H2 performance expected above H1.

INTEREST COST & DEBT
- Finance cost includes supplier credit charges.
- Supplier credit funded working capital during H1.
- Lower reported debt doesn't mean lower financing costs.

MARGIN & PRODUCT MIX
- No aggressive conversion charge increases planned.
- Legacy customer pricing remains unchanged.
- Margins driven by specialised products.
- Key products: HVDC and 765kV wires.
- Exports also support profitability.

CAPACITY EXPANSION
- Specialised wire utilisation already exceeds 80%.
- New capacity trigger has been achieved.
- Phase 3 expansion focused exclusively on specialised wire.
- Phase 3 uses existing land.
- Additional 10 acres offer further expansion.
- Potential additional capacity: 20,000 MT.

DEMAND VISIBILITY
- India CTC demand targets 120–130k MT by FY30.
- Customers have order visibility extending to 2032.
- Customers seeking multi-year supply agreements.
- Hitachi five-year framework volumes settle within two quarters.

IMPORTANT CLARIFICATION
- Lease liability increase relates to upcast plant.
- It is not related to Supa land.
- Additional land supports subsequent capacity expansion.

KEY TAKEAWAY
- Peak realisations should not be extrapolated.
- Specialised products remain the margin driver.
- H2 volumes expected to improve.
- Absolute EBITDA outlook remains intact.

**Arvind Fashions

A few interesting commitments:

→ Mid-double-digit revenue growth for the balance of FY27
→ 30–40 bps EBITDA margin expansion
→ D2C share target of ~65%, from 53% currently
→ H2 free cash flow release of ₹150–175 crore, with a large part intended for debt reduction.
Growth, channel mix and balance-sheet improvement. Worth tracking together.**

**Carborundum Universal Q2

A good example of why segment-level analysis matters.

FY27 guidance:

→ Ceramics growth raised to 25–28%
→ Ceramics margin raised to 22.5–23.5%
→ Abrasives margin lowered to 8–8.5%.
Different segments, different trajectories. Consolidated numbers may not tell the complete story.**

**Tanfac Industries Q2

Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance from 30% to 35–40%.

The bigger story is HFC-32:

→ 2,000–3,000 tonnes volume ramp-up in FY27
→ ~95% utilisation targeted in FY28
→ FY28 EBITDA margin guidance: 24–26%.
A significant capacity ramp-up lies ahead.**

**Dhoot Transmission Q2 

Strong growth ambitions:

→ FY27 revenue growth: 40–45%
→ FY27 capex: ~₹750 crore
→ EBITDA margin: 15–16%
→ Three additional wiring harness plants expected by mid-FY28.
Now, execution and utilisation will be key to watch.**

**GNG Electronics

Management raised its FY27 revenue growth guidance to ~40%.
PAT margin expansion guidance also improved from 100 bps to 150 bps over FY26.
One thing to watch: inventory is expected to remain elevated through Q4 FY27.**

**PRABHUDAS LILLADHER – INDRAPRASTHA GAS (IGL)**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating: Buy.
- Target price revised to ₹161 from ₹165.

**Q2 FY27 Performance**
- EBITDA loss: ₹30 Cr.
- EBITDA missed estimates significantly.
- EBITDA/scm: -₹0.30 vs ₹3.40 in Q1.
- Gas costs increased 22% QoQ, 47.9% YoY.

**Volume Performance**
- Total volumes: 10.1 mmscmd, up 8% YoY.
- CNG volumes: 7.6 mmscmd, up 8.7%.
- PNG volumes: 2.5 mmscmd, up 6%.
- Total volumes grew 4.2% QoQ.

**Margin & Supply Outlook**
- Spot LNG share increased to 15% from 3%.
- Management retains ₹6–7/scm EBITDA guidance.
- Term LNG supplies expected from Q3.
- Further supply additions expected during Q4.
- Targets approximately 10% volume growth.

**Valuation**
- Standalone business valued at 10x Sep'28E EPS.
- Investments valued at ₹21/share.
- Holding company discount: 25%.

**Key Takeaway**
- Higher spot gas costs severely impacted margins.
- Strong volume growth remains encouraging.
- Term LNG recovery is the key catalyst.
- Impact: **Mixed to Positive**

Curious when FII will come back to India

So gave Co-pilot a prompt
“Why FIIs wont return to India even as AI trade unwind globally”

Reverse Psychology

Here is the response

1. India is still expensive vs EM peers
o Even after corrections, India trades at a premium to most emerging markets.
o FIIs compare India with China, Korea, Taiwan, Brazil, not with India's own history.
o If China is at 10-12x PE and India at 20-25x PE, capital tends to chase cheaper markets. 
2. India lacks direct AI beneficiaries
o The AI trade created winners in US tech, Taiwan semiconductors and Korean memory-chip companies.
o India has very few large listed AI, semiconductor or hyperscaler plays that global thematic funds can buy. 
3. Dollar returns matter, not rupee returns
o FIIs think in USD.
o Even if Nifty is flat or slightly up, rupee depreciation can wipe out returns.
o Currency risk remains a major deterrent for foreign capital. 
4. US yields remain a strong competitor
o If US Treasuries offer attractive risk-free returns, FIIs need a much higher expected return from India.
o Many global allocators prefer earning 4-5% in dollar assets rather than taking EM risk. 
5. India's earnings growth has moderated
o India's premium valuation was justified when earnings were compounding rapidly.
o If earnings growth slows while valuations remain rich, FIIs question the risk-reward. 
6. Better opportunities elsewhere
o Korea, Taiwan and China offer exposure to AI, semiconductors and manufacturing at lower valuations.
o Global funds have finite capital; India is competing against these markets for allocation. 
7. India is no longer an under-owned market
o After years of strong inflows, most EM funds already have meaningful India exposure.
o Incremental flows require a new catalyst, not just the absence of AI enthusiasm.
8. Domestic flows reduce urgency
o SIPs, mutual funds and insurance money continue supporting Indian markets despite FII selling.
o Paradoxically, this resilience prevents large valuation corrections that would otherwise attract FIIs back.

Maruti Suzuki India should be rechristened as Suzuki India

Maruti's journey started as a Govt of India project. Maruti Udyog was the Indian promoter & Suzuki was brought in as the technology partner. Back then, this was very much an Indian company with Japanese know-how.

Over time, the Indian promoter gradually diluted its holding & eventually exited completely. Suzuki did the opposite, staying invested through every cycle & steadily increasing its stake.

What began as a JV slowly became Suzuki's most important global asset. The ownership story itself tells you who has deepened commitment over the decades.

For years, investors debated why Suzuki was setting up fresh manufacturing capacity outside Maruti Suzuki through its Gujarat subsidiary instead of housing it directly in the listed entity.

Then came the reversal. Suzuki transferred Suzuki Motor Gujarat into Maruti Suzuki at a valuation of roughly ₹12,000+ Cr. Rather than taking cash, it largely took equity.

The result? Suzuki's ownership in Maruti Suzuki moved up further without having to buy equivalent shares from the secondary market.

This wasn't just a restructuring exercise. It was Suzuki effectively converting manufacturing assets into a larger stake in India's largest PV company.

Even after that transaction, Suzuki did not stop. It has periodically picked up additional shares from the open market whenever opportunities emerged.

The message is clear. The Indian promoter exited long ago. The Japanese promoter keeps doubling down on India.

Look at the cars on the road today. The branding emphasis is on the giant "S" logo. 10-15years back, cars started selling with only “S” logo, 1st on premium nexa cars, then on all the models. You will hardly see Maruti branded cars on road now

For many younger buyers, the brand recall is shifting from "Maruti Suzuki" to simply "Suzuki". The transition is subtle but visible.

India is now the crown jewel of Suzuki Motor Corp. A substantial portion of Suzuki valuation come from Indian listed entity. Maruti $38bn mcap translate to $21bn (for 58% stake, $15bn if applied 30% Holdco disc).

Even beyond that, Maruti pays over $500m to Suzuki as royalty, that value must be over $5bn in the SoTP of Suzuki motors. Suzuki motors also have successful 2w biz in India, they are 6th largest 2w in India, clocking over 1lac units every month

In many ways, investors buying Suzuki Motor Corp are indirectly buying the India story. Cars sold by Suzuki in India is higher than overall car sold by Suzuki in other 100 countries combined

A rebranding to "Suzuki India" could also help shed the old "cheap small-car company" perception. As premium SUVs, hybrids & future EVs gain share, a stronger global MNC identity may command a different customer mindset.

Ownership, capital allocation, manufacturing integration, branding & growth strategy all point in one direction: this is increasingly Suzuki's India story.

Conclusion: Maruti only stays in Co. name hence should be renamed now
